scenarios.why_now: No scale result is credible without a stable and attributable control case.

scenarios.title: Transactional Job State & Idempotency
scenarios.engineering_question: Can 100 to 500 concurrent mutations commit one legal and idempotent outcome?
scenarios.why_now: Durable state correctness must precede retries and queued high-volume mutation.
scenarios.observed_gap: The earlier store-level concurrency proof stopped at concurrency 64 and simulated lease time. It did not prove measured 100/250/500 external HTTP concurrency, bounded pool failure through the API, exact worker PID loss, non-vacuous effects, or PostgreSQL-to-JSON mirror recovery.
proposed_design: Use database transactions and unique idempotency keys for every state mutation.
Enforce legal transitions, atomic lease claims, fencing, and stale-owner reconciliation.
Bound connection-pool size and wait time and expose conflict outcomes as telemetry.

changed_components.component: Existing lifecycle state and worker ownership
Existing task, deployment, and side-effect boundaries

implementation_summary: A dedicated PostgreSQL 16 control-plane database and schema own concurrent lifecycle, task, deployment, claim, idempotency, and outbox records.
Database-unique idempotency keys, legal optimistic transitions, atomic lease claims, monotonic fencing, and stale-owner reconciliation fail closed.
External API middleware measures process-level current and peak in-flight requests with bounded-cardinality metrics.

The existing supervised lifecycle worker supports an isolated run-scoped proof: exact claim hold, OS process loss, replacement claim, stale-owner fence, one-time effects, and database-authoritative mirror reconciliation.
Dual reads remain database-first while the JSON rollback mirror and explicit file-mode rollback path are retained.
Rejected preflights and regression failures are retained in the closure RCA; only the final revision and fresh evidence close S1.
scenarios.experiment_environment: Fresh external TCP/HTTP API processes, real supervised worker processes, and PostgreSQL 16 isolated schemas on the existing local single-node runtime. No production serving, GPU, device-plugin, customer data, MLflow database, or Airflow database mutation occurred.
test_or_experiment_steps: Call the live lifecycle create, approve, cancel, and retry API routes from an external client at measured peak in-flight 100, 250, and 500.
Exhaust a one-connection PostgreSQL pool through the live API and measure bounded 503 responses and timeout telemetry.
Wait until the supervisor reports the exact worker PID live while that worker owns claim epoch 1, then terminate that PID at the OS boundary.
Observe a different process claim epoch 2, block the stale epoch-1 commit, and commit one terminal lifecycle outcome plus one lifecycle, deployment, and artifact effect each.
Inject a PostgreSQL-commit-to-JSON-mirror gap, then require restarted-worker reconciliation and payload/version parity.
Drop all isolated schemas and remove all run-scoped worker processes before accepting the evidence.

acceptance_criteria.description: A real worker commits at least one lifecycle, deployment, and artifact effect, and each required effect is committed exactly once with duplicate count zero.
External create, approve, cancel, and retry conflicts at measured peak in-flight 100, 250, and 500 end in one legal database outcome.
Pool exhaustion through the external API returns a bounded observable failure rather than hanging.
Exact worker process loss advances the fencing epoch, blocks the stale owner, commits one terminal outcome, and restores PostgreSQL/JSON payload and version parity.

scenarios.observed_result: S1 passed at revision 8a8f54c. External HTTP sweeps reached measured client/server peak in-flight 100/100, 250/250, and 500/500 with 100/100, 250/250, and 500/500 completions, zero transport timeouts, complete request/trace identity, and one legal outcome for every conflict. A one-connection pool returned 12/12 bounded 503 responses within 0.328 seconds. The exact epoch-1 worker PID was terminated; the supervisor launched a different process, epoch 2 fenced the stale owner, one terminal commit and one lifecycle/deployment/artifact effect each were recorded with zero duplicates, and the injected PostgreSQL-to-JSON mirror gap was reconciled to payload/version parity in at most 9.875 seconds.

External HTTP peak-concurrency 100/250/500, bounded API pool failure, and actual supervised worker-loss evidence passed S1-AC-01 through S1-AC-04.
Strict S1 closure records superseded evidence, non-vacuous effects, PostgreSQL/JSON parity, rejected attempts, tests, cleanup, residual risks, and claim limits.

scenarios.title: Bounded Queue & Backpressure
scenarios.engineering_question: Does overload stay memory-bounded while accepted work reaches an explicit outcome?
scenarios.why_now: A bounded queue is required before capacity and recovery experiments scale up.
scenarios.observed_gap: The prior S2 closure did not persist every V3 bound and wait signal or independently recompute acceptance from numeric evidence; its 30-profile result is retained as historical baseline only until a fresh strict-evidence rerun passes.
proposed_design: Combine a durable queue with a bounded process-local async queue and semaphore.
Bound depth, bytes, age, and time; reject excess work with Retry-After.
Retry only transient failures with backoff, jitter, and a global budget; isolate poison work.
Scale CPU workers from queue telemetry while keeping the GPU worker count at one.
implementation_summary: The existing task create and confirmation boundaries now reserve durable PostgreSQL queue capacity atomically with idempotency and task collection state when durable mode is enabled.
Accepted idempotency replay returns the original task without another depth or byte reservation; rejected capacity does not reserve the key.
Canonical UTF-8 item size fails with 413 while aggregate depth or byte pressure fails with 429 and an integer Retry-After.
A dedicated bounded task queue worker, separate from the lifecycle worker, claims with SKIP LOCKED and owner/epoch leases, enforces local count and byte budgets, and applies retry/DLQ policy.
Durable task dispatch releases the legacy operations-ledger advisory and file lock before external Airflow HTTP, while fenced row-level PostgreSQL ownership protects the task and effect commit.
Terminal queue, effect, and task detail rows are compacted under frozen row and age limits into fixed-cardinality rollups; the JSON task collection is retained only as a bounded rollback mirror.

The operational-safety checkpoint adds bounded pre-FastAPI ingress, approval-state bounds, idempotency tombstones, deadline and effect fencing, fair runtime polling, evidence-backed outcome_unknown handling, cutover and rollback parity, exact parent-bound executor cleanup, portable process-tree RSS, and globally bounded downstream GPU work.

The first clean strict run exposed a real CPU downstream-cap bypass and a worker-restart queue-wait evidence gap. A rejected deterministic submission is now reset to reserved only after absence is proven; ambiguous effects move directly to outcome_unknown, and pre-restart queue-wait histograms are retained for final evidence.

The external E/G/H preflight confirmed queue-wait count 520 for every E repetition, CPU downstream peaks at or below 8, and 20 transient G items in DLQ. Its first G run exposed a projection-only reason-precedence bug; retry-budget and attempts-exhausted terminal reasons now take precedence over their generic last failure class.

At strict-evidence revision e5b399a, the frozen A-J external matrix completed 30 of 30 profile repetitions with all four acceptance criteria and all 11 readiness gates passed. 61 focused real-PostgreSQL tests, 692 full Python tests, 59 Control Panel tests, and the production frontend build also passed. All acceptance values were recomputed from persisted numeric evidence rather than stored pass flags.

At strict-evidence revision e5b399a, the frozen A-J external matrix completed 30 of 30 profile repetitions with all four acceptance criteria and all 11 readiness gates passed. 61 focused real-PostgreSQL tests, 692 full Python tests, 59 Control Panel tests, and the production frontend build also passed. All acceptance values were recomputed from persisted numeric evidence rather than stored pass flags.

No customer traffic or production endpoint was used.

Measure queue age, bytes, API and worker process-tree RSS, terminal closure, rejection, retry, DLQ, trace continuity, effect identity, cleanup, and GPU external runtime concurrency.

scenarios.title: Dependency Soak & Resource-efficiency Closure
scenarios.engineering_question: Do bounded retries and selected operating points remain stable during faults and soak?
scenarios.why_now: Closure requires long-run resource trends and dependency recovery after isolated passes.
scenarios.observed_gap: Retry amplification, resource slope, efficiency, and final re-hash are unproven.
proposed_design: Inject service-scoped latency or timeout with bounded proxy or deterministic fixtures.
Enforce retry budget, exponential backoff, jitter, circuit hold, and queue drain.
Run a 30 to 60 minute soak near the selected safe operating point.
Calculate CPU/GPU time efficiency and re-hash every accepted evidence artifact.
implementation_summary: Implementation has not started.
scenarios.experiment_environment: Not exercised. Planned scope is a generalized local single-node container and Kubernetes runtime with one accelerator where required.
test_or_experiment_steps: Validate one dependency fault at a time and prove cleanup before the next.
Run the cross-layer soak only after every isolated scenario has passed.
Measure amplification, recovery, resource slopes, efficiency, integrity, and residual risk.

acceptance_criteria.description: Retry amplification stays within the declared budget.
Memory, file descriptor, pool, queue, and artifact slopes remain bounded.
MTTR, request impact, efficiency Pareto, and residual risk are recorded.
One final evidence index re-hashes every accepted result.

selection_reasons: Run dependency faults and soak only after isolated correctness and capacity boundaries are accepted.

compatibility: Existing A-E guard evidence remains baseline-only and cannot substitute for fresh scale-soak evidence.
migration: Introduce fault controls behind explicit profiles and retain a no-fault operating profile for rollback.

preconditions: S0 through S7 have accepted evidence, cleanup proof, and one selected safe operating point.
experiment_contract.workload_input: One bounded dependency fault at a time followed by a 30-60 minute controlled replay near 70 percent of measured sustainable capacity.
procedure: Validate one dependency fault at a time and prove cleanup before the next.
Run the cross-layer soak only after every isolated scenario has passed.
Measure amplification, recovery, resource slopes, efficiency, integrity, and residual risk.
controlled_variables: Dependency target, fault latency/duration, timeout, retry budget, backoff, jitter, circuit hold, and load rate.
signals: Retry amplification, MTTR, request impact, memory/FD/pool/queue slopes, CPU/GPU time, efficiency, cleanup, and evidence hashes.
acceptance_criteria: Retry amplification stays within the declared budget.
Memory, file descriptor, pool, queue, and artifact slopes remain bounded.
MTTR, request impact, efficiency Pareto, and residual risk are recorded.
One final evidence index re-hashes every accepted result.
stop_conditions: Fault scope escapes the target, retry budget is exceeded, resource slope is unbounded, or cleanup becomes uncertain.
recovery_conditions: Fault is removed, dependencies and queues recover, resources return to baseline, and every accepted artifact re-hashes.
